current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2024 (2nd Sess. 157th G.A.), 2025 (1st Sess. 158th) and 2026 (2nd Sess. 158th) via the Office of Legislative Counsel 'Summary of General Statutes Enacted' for each year (opened). Only 2025 SB 12 (Act 276, eff. May 14, 2025) amended O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71, and per the Legislative Counsel summary and Senate Research Office synopsis it revised subsection (a) (requests made upon the custodian; retrieval of records held by private entities) — the enrolled text could not be opened from legis.ga.gov (JS-only bill pages; API returned 401/500), so the (a) change is noted for manual verification but is outside the fee subsections. § 50-18-72 was amended in 2024 and 2026 without fee content; § 50-18-75 was reserved in 2026. Fee subsections (c) and (d) of § 50-18-71 and § 50-18-77 have not been amended since Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); a Justia rendering of the 2024 code (opened via Wayback) shows only technical 2013/2021 amendments and the 2016 (d.1) athletics clause. Codified text: Georgia's official annotated code is on LexisNexis (not fetchable); the operative fee text was opened verbatim from the Georgia Public Library Service statute PDF (current through 2017 — accurate for (c)/(d)) and cross-checked against the statute appendix of the AG-hosted Sunshine Laws guide (6th ed. 2019) and the Justia 2024 rendering. Guidance-vs-law gaps: three fee propositions exist only in guidance/case law, not statute — no fee for mere inspection of routinely-inspectable records (McFrugal Rental v. Garr), no charge for attorney disclosure-review time (Trammell v. Martin), and 'mailing' as a chargeable administrative cost / discretionary waiver (AG-approved LE guide 2014). Georgia has no administrative rule implementing ORA fees for local governments and no delegation of any fee figure to another instrument; all figures are statutory and bind municipalities directly. law.georgia.gov and law.justia.com returned 403 to direct fetches; the AG guides were opened through the Internet Archive captures of the official law.georgia.gov URLs.

resolutions.unit: USD per page (letter or legal size)
resolutions.source_language: In addition to a charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records, an agency may charge a fee for the copying of records or data, not to exceed 10¢ per page for letter or legal size documents or, in the case of other documents, the actual cost of producing the copy.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
resolutions.notes: Statutory cap; city sets the operative per-page value at or under 10¢ for letter/legal pages. Operative verb is 'may charge ... not to exceed' (Permission with ceiling); GA-9001 amends GA-0018's rule_type from Requirement to Permission and cleans a stray '$0.25' remark in its notes. 'Agency' (§ 50-18-70(b)(1) via § 50-14-1(a)(1)(B)-(C)) includes every county, municipal corporation, school district and their departments, so the figure binds municipalities directly; Georgia runs a single regime for state and local bodies.

resolutions.unit: USD per page (letter or legal size, any ink)
resolutions.source_language: In addition to a charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records, an agency may charge a fee for the copying of records or data, not to exceed 10¢ per page for letter or legal size documents or, in the case of other documents, the actual cost of producing the copy.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
resolutions.manual_verification: Scope judgment: statute distinguishes only by page size (letter/legal vs 'other documents'), not by color; a color letter/legal copy therefore falls under the 10¢ cap. No AG guidance found addressing color specifically.
resolutions.notes: No separate color rate exists in Georgia law; the 10¢ cap is size-based. Non-letter/legal color output falls under 'actual cost of producing the copy'.

Where fees for certified copies or other copies or records are specifically authorized or otherwise prescribed by law, such specific fee shall apply when certified copies or other records to which a specific fee may apply are sought.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)

No general municipal specialty schedule exists in Georgia law.
resolutions.notes: Transcripts: none addressed in ORA. AG-approved LE guide sample estimate shows '$3/print' photographs and '$10/copy' videotape but those are illustrative sample figures, not law, and were not extracted.

resolutions.unit: USD per hour (formula ceiling; no statewide dollar figure)
resolutions.source_language: In all other instances, the charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid full-time employee who, in the reasonable discretion of the custodian of the records, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request; provided, however, that no charge shall be made for the first quarter hour.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
resolutions.notes: The state supplies a formula ceiling, not a number; the city computes its operative rate from its own payroll (salary only). Also bounded by the 'reasonable charge' / 'most economical means' standard in (c)(1). 'Agency' (§ 50-18-70(b)(1) via § 50-14-1(a)(1)(B)-(C)) includes every county, municipal corporation, school district and their departments, so the figure binds municipalities directly; Georgia runs a single regime for state and local bodies.

An agency also may not charge for time its attorneys spend advising whether records should be disclosed.

resolutions.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
resolutions.notes: Statutory trigger the city cannot move: above $25.00 the agency 'shall notify the requester ... not to exceed three business days' with the estimate. Structural companion (GA-0023): search/retrieval may be deferred until the requester agrees to pay. 'Agency' (§ 50-18-70(b)(1) via § 50-14-1(a)(1)(B)-(C)) includes every county, municipal corporation, school district and their departments, so the figure binds municipalities directly; Georgia runs a single regime for state and local bodies.

resolutions.notes: No deadline for the requester to accept an estimate and no deemed-withdrawal after N days; the agency may simply defer search and retrieval 'until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs' (GA-0023). resolutions.unit: USD (estimated costs for production of the records)
resolutions.source_language: In any instance in which the estimated costs for production of the records exceeds $500.00, an agency may insist on prepayment of the costs prior to beginning search, retrieval, review, or production of the records.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
resolutions.notes: Above $500.00 the agency 'may insist on prepayment of the costs' before beginning search, retrieval, review or production. Below that threshold prepayment cannot be insisted upon, though search/retrieval may still be deferred pending agreement to pay once the estimate exceeds $25 (GA-0023). Threshold is fixed by statute; the city only chooses whether to exercise the permission. 'Agency' (§ 50-18-70(b)(1) via § 50-14-1(a)(1)(B)-(C)) includes every county, municipal corporation, school district and their departments, so the figure binds municipalities directly; Georgia runs a single regime for state and local bodies.

resolutions.source_language: In any instance in which the estimated costs for production of the records exceeds $500.00, an agency may insist on prepayment of the costs prior to beginning search, retrieval, review, or production of the records.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
resolutions.manual_verification: The statute authorizes 'prepayment of the costs' (i.e., the estimated costs) without stating a fraction; read literally the whole estimate may be required. Not recorded as a 100% value because no percentage is stated.
resolutions.notes: No cap or floor on the prepayment fraction; the permission is framed as prepayment of the estimated costs. resolutions.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs. In any instance in which the estimated costs for production of the records exceeds $500.00, an agency may insist on prepayment of the costs prior to beginning search, retrieval, review, or production of the records. Whenever any person has requested to inspect or copy a public record and does not pay the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully estimated and agreed to pursuant to this article, and the agency has incurred the agreed-upon costs to make the records available, regardless of whether the requester inspects or accepts copies of the records, the agency shall be authorized to collect such charges in any manner authorized by law for the collection of taxes, fees, or assessments by such agency.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
resolutions.notes: Three gates the engine must be able to execute; none is a city-filled value. Note the (c)(3) collection right applies only to charges 'lawfully estimated and agreed to' — the estimate/agreement step is a precondition to collection.

resolutions.value: prior_unpaid_costs -> may require prepayment for all future requests until paid or dispute resolved; no deemed-withdrawal-after-N-days rule
resolutions.source_language: Whenever any person who has requested to inspect or copy a public record has not paid the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully incurred, an agency may require prepayment for compliance with all future requests for production of records from that person until the costs for the prior production of records have been paid or the dispute regarding payment resolved. Whenever any person has requested to inspect or copy a public record and does not pay the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully estimated and agreed to pursuant to this article, and the agency has incurred the agreed-upon costs to make the records available, regardless of whether the requester inspects or accepts copies of the records, the agency shall be authorized to collect such charges in any manner authorized by law for the collection of taxes, fees, or assessments by such agency.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)
resolutions.notes: Georgia has no N-day nonpayment withdrawal clock; the consequences are (i) requester-level prepayment gating for future requests (GA-0025) and (ii) collection of agreed, incurred costs 'in any manner authorized by law for the collection of taxes, fees, or assessments' (GA-0026).

resolutions.value: pause: agency may defer search and retrieval until requester agrees to pay (>$25) or prepays (>$500); while search/retrieval is so delayed, the exemption-notice deadline shifts to 3 business days after the records have been retrieved; no grace period or lapse action stated

In any instance in which an agency is required to or has decided to withhold all or part of a requested record, the agency shall notify the requester of the specific legal authority exempting the requested record or records from disclosure by Code section, subsection, and paragraph within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days or in the event the search and retrieval of records is delayed pursuant to this subsection or pursuant to subparagraph (b)(1)(A) of this Code section, then no later than three business days after the records have been retrieved.

resolutions.notes: The clock effect is a pause on search/retrieval; the only downstream re-anchoring stated in text is the withholding-notice deadline ('no later than three business days after the records have been retrieved' when search and retrieval is delayed pursuant to this subsection). No statutory grace period or automatic lapse/closure for an unpaid prepayment. The re-anchoring clause may already be captured in GA's denial-notice rows; not duplicated as a new fee row.

resolutions.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)

new_rules.legal_concept: Copy charge capped at 10 cents per page (letter/legal); other sizes at actual cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may charge a copying fee not to exceed 10 cents per page for letter or legal size documents or, for other documents, the actual cost of producing the copy.
new_rules.source_language: In addition to a charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records, an agency may charge a fee for the copying of records or data, not to exceed 10¢ per page for letter or legal size documents or, in the case of other documents, the actual cost of producing the copy.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (fee subsections (c)-(d) last substantively amended by Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); confirmed unamended through the 2026 session)

Substance unchanged: ceiling $0.10/page letter/legal; actual cost for other document sizes. Confirmed unamended through the 2026 session via Legislative Counsel summaries.

new_rules.legal_concept: ORA procedures and fees do not apply to investigative requests from grand juries, taxing authorities, law enforcement or prosecutors
new_rules.atomic_rule: The ORA's procedures and fees do not apply to public records requested in writing by a state or federal grand jury, taxing authority, law enforcement agency, or prosecuting attorney in conjunction with an ongoing administrative, criminal, or tax investigation; the custodian shall provide copies to the requesting agency unless privileged or restricted by law.
new_rules.trigger: Written request from a grand jury, taxing authority, law enforcement agency or prosecuting attorney in conjunction with an ongoing administrative, criminal or tax investigation
new_rules.source_language: The procedures and fees provided for in this article shall not apply to public records, including records that are exempt from disclosure pursuant to Code Section 50-18-72, which are requested in writing by a state or federal grand jury, taxing authority, law enforcement agency, or prosecuting attorney in conjunction with an ongoing administrative, criminal, or tax investigation. The lawful custodian shall provide copies of such records to the requesting agency unless such records are privileged or disclosure to such agencies is specifically restricted by law.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (enacted Ga. L. 1999, p. 809; amended Ga. L. 2012, p. 218 (HB 397); no 2024–2026 amendment)
new_rules.notes: Mandatory no-fee (and no-ORA-procedure) category for a class of governmental requesters; routes such requests out of the fee engine entirely. Text opened in the AG-hosted Sunshine Laws guide appendix (statute reproduction) and cross-checked against the 2024–2026 Legislative Counsel summaries.

new_rules.legal_concept: No fee for mere inspection of routinely-inspectable records
new_rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged when a person seeks only to inspect records that are routinely subject to public inspection (e.g., deeds, city ordinances, zoning maps).
new_rules.trigger: Requester seeks only to inspect a record routinely subject to public inspection
new_rules.source_language: The Georgia Supreme Court has held that no fee may be charged when a person seeks only to inspect records that are routinely subject to public inspection, such as deeds, city ordinances and zoning maps.
new_rules.source_authority: AG/GFAF 'Sunshine Laws: A Guide to Open Government in Georgia' (6th ed., June 2019) p. 5, restating McFrugal Rental of Riverdale v. Garr, 262 Ga. 369 (1992)
new_rules.notes: Guidance restating a Georgia Supreme Court holding; the opinion itself was not opened. Guide is published by the Georgia First Amendment Foundation 'in cooperation with' and hosted by the Office of the Attorney General. Human legal review recommended before treating as a hard gate.

new_rules.legal_concept: No charge for attorney time spent advising whether records should be disclosed
new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may not charge for time its attorneys spend advising whether records should be disclosed.

new_rules.source_language: An agency also may not charge for time its attorneys spend advising whether records should be disclosed.
